turns.doctor_question: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hello, Dr. Smith. It's very nice to meet you, and thank you so much for taking the time to see me. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your day. 

Um... I guess I'm here because... well, it's a little embarrassing to talk about, to be honest, and I really don't want you to think badly of me. But for nearly two years now, I've just been so sure that our contractor and, well, some of the people on my block, are quietly working together to cheat us. They're keeping my kitchen half-wrong on purpose, and it's just been very stressful. 

My husband keeps showing me all these receipts to try and make me feel better, and the workers always have so many excuses, but... I just know what they're doing. I hope that makes sense? I really don't want to sound like a difficult person or a complainer, I just don't know what else to do. Am I explaining that okay?

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed, unyielding belief that her contractor and neighbors are conspiring against her, despite contradictory evidence like receipts.

turns.doctor_question: If you were to see definitive, indisputable evidence that the contractor was not cheating you, would you be able to accept that you were mistaken?
turns.patient_response:
Oh... well... I want to say yes. I really, really do. I know that's what I should say, and I'd love nothing more than to just... put this all behind me and tell my husband he was right all along. 

But... oh, doctor, if I'm being perfectly honest with you—and I do want to be a good patient and give you the truth—it's just... well, it's been nearly two years. Two whole years of feeling this way. And even with all the receipts my husband brings me, and all the excuses the workers give... I just can't shake this certainty I have. It just feels so clear to me that the contractor, and maybe a few of the neighbors, are quietly working together to cheat us. To just... keep the kitchen half-wrong on purpose. 

I know that sounds so stubborn, and I'm so sorry. I really don't want to be a difficult person. But even if you showed me something that looked like perfect proof...
